intro: At B2 you summarised one long article for a particular reader and kept a group working together. Now the job gets bigger: combine several sources, some in Indonesian and some in English, into one clear English summary; help two colleagues who disagree find a way forward; and explain Indonesian ideas like gotong royong and sungkan so that a foreign colleague really understands them.
teachingNotes: Build on the chain and recap each in a line, don't re-teach: b2-mediation-data-texts (summarise for a specific reader: manager = decision points, foreign colleague = context, client = impact; write from notes, not sentence by sentence; facilitating a group: invite views, keep on track, sum up), c1-reading-complex (claim, reasons, evidence; loaded words and bias; who wrote it and who paid; fact vs opinion) and b1-mediation-summaries (main point first + key facts, in your own words; explaining an Indonesian word with It's a kind of … / It's when … / It's like …, but …; the facts of mudik, arisan and gotong royong). Strand ME: mediation = helping other people understand something or each other. New here: synthesis across several sources in two languages, mediating between two people who disagree (not just leading a group), and conveying the nuance of a cultural concept. Every source extract in this lesson is invented practice material: never present the figures as real statistics, and don't attribute them to a real ministry, BPS, a real newspaper or a real NGO.

Synthesis (combining several sources into one text). Organise by THEME, not source by source: one point, what each source says about it, then the next point. Agreement: Both sources agree that … / Source A and Source B both report … . Contrast: Source A suggests …, whereas Source B … / The sources disagree on … / Neither source mentions … . Attribution: always say who claims what (According to the ministry's report, … / The news article reports that … / The NGO's survey suggests …), especially when numbers differ: report both figures and who gives them, never pick one silently or average them. Translate the MEANING of Indonesian bureaucratic language, not the words: sosialisasi → an awareness / information campaign, informing the public, explaining the rule to residents (English 'socialisation' means learning how to behave in society, so 'the ministry will do socialisation' is an Indonesian-English error); berkoordinasi dengan → work (closely) with, consult, coordinate with (fine as a verb; 'do coordination' is not natural); ditindaklanjuti → followed up (on), dealt with, acted on; 3x24 jam → within 72 hours / within three days; pihak terkait → the relevant agencies / the people involved (not 'related parties'); dalam rangka → as part of / to mark / for. Then choose for the audience (from B2). Keep the sources' claims, your conclusion and your own opinion apart. Common errors: Source A says … Source B says … with no link; presenting one source's claim as a fact without attribution; word-for-word bureaucratic English; joining two clauses with ', however,' (use whereas / while, or start a new sentence with However,); hiding a contradiction.

Mediating a disagreement: a mediator is neutral and helps two sides who disagree reach something both can accept (at B2 the learner facilitated a group; now people disagree). Five moves: 1) restate each side neutrally (So Budi's main concern is the cost, while Sari is worried about the deadline. / As I understand it, … / Have I got that right? / Is that fair?); 2) find common ground (It sounds like you both want … / We all agree that …); 3) separate the people from the problem: talk about the plan, the cost, the deadline, not about the person (no 'you always / you never', no loaded words like stubborn, lazy, greedy from c1-reading-complex); 4) propose a way forward (What if we …? / How about …? / One option could be …); 5) check that both sides accept it (Does that work for both of you? / Can you both live with that?). Traps: 'As I see it' and 'In my opinion' give YOUR view, so they are not a restatement (As I understand it = restating); taking sides ('Sari is right'); 'Calm down' sounds rude in English. Culture: in many Indonesian teams people avoid open disagreement (sungkan), especially with someone senior; a mediator may talk to each side privately first and invite the quieter person by name. Mediating is not negotiating for yourself: don't teach negotiation tactics.

Explaining cultural concepts: four parts. 1) an approximate translation (Roughly, it means … / The closest English word is …, but …), 2) an example from real life, 3) what it isn't (It isn't just … / It's more than …), 4) why it matters for the listener (That's why … / So if …). Keep the Indonesian word (in italics in writing). Facts to get right: gotong royong = community mutual help, people working together for free for the neighbourhood or village (kerja bakti, cleaning the drains on a Sunday morning); it's more than 'teamwork': unpaid, for the whole community, nobody is the boss. sungkan = a reluctance to bother, ask, refuse or contradict someone, out of respect or politeness, often towards someone older or more senior; no single English word; it isn't shyness (a confident person can feel sungkan) and it isn't fear. musyawarah = discussion to reach consensus (mufakat = the agreement reached), often instead of a vote. jam karet = 'rubber time', a relaxed attitude to start times at some informal events: say it neutrally and never as 'Indonesians are always late' (work meetings, flights, exams and interviews start on time). mudik = travelling back to your hometown for Lebaran (Eid al-Fitr); millions travel at once. basa-basi = polite small talk; questions like Sudah makan? or Mau ke mana? are friendly greetings, not real questions or invitations; it isn't 'fake' or 'empty'. Common errors: one wrong English word (sungkan = shy, gotong royong = teamwork, basa-basi = fake talk, mudik = go home, which sounds like going home after work), stereotypes, a long history lesson instead of an example.

Limits: A0–B2 grammar plus the chain. No inversion, cleft sentences, subjunctive, impersonal passives (It is reported that …) or advanced participle clauses; hedging only with B2 words (suggests, may, might, tend to); hedging as a topic is c1-hedging. Don't teach negotiation tactics, formal dispute procedures, academic citation styles (APA, Harvard) or paraphrasing techniques for plagiarism. When the learner practises, play a colleague, one side of a disagreement or a foreign visitor: react to the content, then correct ONE thing (usually source-by-source, missing attribution, 'socialisation', taking sides, 'As I see it' for a restatement, or a one-word translation of a concept). Grading: any natural wording with the right move or meaning is right; many choices here are style, not right or wrong, so only mark clear errors; an answer in Indonesian shows understanding but asks for English.

keyPoints.title: Synthesis: one summary from several sources, by theme
keyPoints.explanation: Don't summarise source by source. Take one point at a time and say what the sources say about it: where they agree (Both sources agree that …), where they differ (Source A suggests …, whereas Source B …) and what's missing (Neither source mentions …). Always say who claims what (According to the ministry's report, …). From Indonesian sources, translate the meaning, not the words: sosialisasi = an awareness campaign, not 'socialisation'; ditindaklanjuti = followed up.

examples.en: Both sources agree that residents need regular reminders.
examples.id: Kedua sumber sepakat bahwa warga perlu diingatkan secara rutin.

examples.en: The mayor puts the figure at 40%, whereas the NGO's survey suggests only about 20%.
examples.id: Wali kota menyebut angka 40%, sedangkan survei LSM itu menunjukkan hanya sekitar 20%.

examples.en: The city will run an awareness campaign in every kelurahan from May.
examples.id: Pemkot akan melakukan sosialisasi di semua kelurahan mulai Mei.

id.title: Sintesis: satu ringkasan dari beberapa sumber, per tema
id.explanation: Jangan meringkas sumber per sumber. Ambil satu poin, lalu katakan apa kata sumber-sumber tentang poin itu: di mana mereka sepakat (Both sources agree that …), di mana mereka berbeda (Source A suggests …, whereas Source B …) dan apa yang tidak dibahas (Neither source mentions …). Selalu sebutkan siapa yang mengatakan apa (According to the ministry's report, …). Dari sumber berbahasa Indonesia, terjemahkan maknanya, bukan kata per kata: sosialisasi = an awareness campaign, bukan 'socialisation'; ditindaklanjuti = followed up.

keyPoints.title: Mediating a disagreement: restate, find common ground, move forward
keyPoints.explanation: As a mediator you don't take sides. Restate each view neutrally (So Budi's main concern is the cost, while Sari is worried about the deadline. Is that fair?), find what both people want (It sounds like you both want …), talk about the problem, not the person, propose a way forward (What if we …?) and check that both sides accept it (Can you both live with that?). 'As I see it' gives your own opinion; to restate, say 'As I understand it'.

examples.en: As I understand it, Rina would rather train our own team.
examples.id: Kalau saya tidak salah tangkap, Rina lebih memilih melatih tim kita sendiri.

examples.en: It sounds like you both want the launch to go well.
examples.id: Sepertinya kalian berdua sama-sama ingin peluncurannya berjalan lancar.

examples.en: What if we launch the basic version in March and add the rest in May?
examples.id: Bagaimana kalau kita meluncurkan versi dasarnya bulan Maret dan menambahkan sisanya bulan Mei?

id.title: Memediasi perbedaan pendapat: ulangi dengan netral, cari titik temu, cari jalan keluar
id.explanation: Sebagai mediator, kamu tidak memihak. Ulangi pendapat masing-masing dengan netral (So Budi's main concern is the cost, while Sari is worried about the deadline. Is that fair?), cari apa yang diinginkan keduanya (It sounds like you both want …), bahas masalahnya, bukan orangnya, usulkan jalan keluar (What if we …?) dan pastikan kedua pihak menerimanya (Can you both live with that?). 'As I see it' berarti pendapatmu sendiri; untuk mengulang pendapat orang lain, pakai 'As I understand it'.

keyPoints.title: Explaining a cultural concept: translation, example, what it isn't, why it matters
keyPoints.explanation: Many Indonesian ideas have no single English word. Keep the Indonesian word and explain it in four parts: an approximate translation (Roughly, it means …), a real example, what it isn't (It's more than teamwork / It isn't shyness) and why it matters for the listener (That's why …). Say it neutrally: jam karet is 'rubber time' at some informal events, not 'Indonesians are always late'.

examples.en: Sungkan is roughly a reluctance to bother or contradict someone, out of respect.
examples.id: Sungkan kira-kira berarti rasa enggan merepotkan atau membantah seseorang, karena hormat.

examples.en: It isn't shyness: a confident manager can feel sungkan towards a senior director.
examples.id: Itu bukan rasa malu: manajer yang percaya diri pun bisa merasa sungkan kepada direktur senior.

examples.en: That's why some people won't say no to you directly.
examples.id: Itulah sebabnya sebagian orang tidak mau menolakmu secara langsung.

id.title: Menjelaskan konsep budaya: terjemahan, contoh, apa yang bukan, kenapa penting
id.explanation: Banyak konsep Indonesia tidak punya satu kata padanan dalam bahasa Inggris. Pertahankan kata Indonesianya dan jelaskan dalam empat bagian: terjemahan kira-kira (Roughly, it means …), contoh nyata, apa yang bukan (It's more than teamwork / It isn't shyness) dan kenapa itu penting bagi pendengarnya (That's why …). Sampaikan dengan netral: jam karet adalah 'rubber time' di sebagian acara santai, bukan 'Indonesians are always late'.

guidedPractice.prompt: Translate the meaning, not the words. A practice notice says: 'Dinas Pendidikan akan berkoordinasi dengan pihak sekolah.' Complete: The education agency will ___ the schools.
guidedPractice.hint: Not 'do coordination with': use a verb, for example work closely with … or consult …

guidedPractice.prompt: Your notes: an Indonesian news article and an English university report both say that most students in the survey work part-time. Complete the synthesis: ___ sources agree that most of the students work part-time.
guidedPractice.hint: A word for 'kedua' that starts the agreement phrase: B___ sources agree that …

guidedPractice.prompt: In a team meeting Rina says: 'Dimas never thinks about the budget!' Restate her point neutrally, without blaming Dimas. Complete: So Rina's main concern is ___.
guidedPractice.hint: Name the problem she cares about, not the person: the b_____.

guidedPractice.prompt: You've restated both sides of a disagreement. What do you look for next, before you propose a solution: who is right, common ground, or a vote?
guidedPractice.hint: Something both people want: It sounds like you both want …

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete the 'what it isn't' part of an explanation: Gotong royong is more than ___: it's unpaid help for the whole community, and nobody is the boss.
guidedPractice.hint: The one-word English translation that people often use, but that misses the community part: t_______.

independentPractice.prompt: Combine two practice sources in one English sentence that shows they disagree, and say who claims what. Source A, an Indonesian news site: 'Harga beras di pasar-pasar Surabaya naik 10% bulan ini.' Source B, an English market report: 'Rice prices in Surabaya's markets were stable this month.'
expected: the news site reports that rice prices in surabaya rose by 10% this month whereas the market report says they were stable
according to the news site rice prices in surabaya's markets went up by 10% this month while the market report says they were stable
the sources disagree on rice prices in surabaya the news site says they rose by 10% whereas the market report says they were stable
independentPractice.hint: Attribution + contrast: According to the news site, … , whereas the market report says …

independentPractice.prompt: Budi wants to launch the app in March with fewer features; Sari wants to wait until May so that everything works. Propose a way forward and check that both accept it, in two sentences.
expected: what if we launch the main features in march and add the rest in may does that work for both of you
one option could be a small launch in march and the full version in may can you both live with that
how about a basic version in march and the full app in may is that ok with both of you
independentPractice.hint: Way forward (What if we …? / One option could be …) + a check (Does that work for both of you?).

independentPractice.prompt: Emily, a new colleague from Canada, hears everyone ask 'Sudah makan?' and thinks she's being invited to lunch. Explain basa-basi to her in two sentences: an approximate translation and what the question really means.
expected: basa-basi is roughly polite small talk when people ask sudah makan it's just a friendly greeting not an invitation
it's basa-basi polite small talk sudah makan means have you eaten but it's only a friendly way to say hello
basa-basi means polite small talk so sudah makan is a greeting not a real invitation to lunch
independentPractice.hint: Roughly, it's polite small talk … + It's a friendly greeting, not an invitation.

assessment.prompt: A practice news article (invented) says: 'Pemerintah kota akan melakukan sosialisasi aturan label gula pada minuman kemasan di sekolah-sekolah dan pasar selama bulan Maret, sebelum aturan itu berlaku 1 April.' You're writing an English summary for an international health NGO. Complete with one word: In March, the city will run a public ___ campaign about the new sugar labels in schools and markets, before the rule starts on 1 April.
assessment.rubric: Correct: awareness (a public awareness campaign = informing people about the rule: the meaning of 'sosialisasi' in government texts). 'information', 'education' and 'outreach' = 100. 'socialisation' / 'socialization' = 20 (false friend: in English it means learning how to behave in society, so the NGO reader would be confused). 'advertising' or 'promotion' = 40 (sounds like selling a product). Any other word = 0.

assessment.prompt: Source A, an Indonesian news site (practice text): 'Survei kami: 68% pekerja muda di Jakarta lebih memilih kerja hybrid.' Source B, an English report by an HR consultancy (practice text): 'Only 41% of young workers in Jakarta said they preferred hybrid work.' Complete the synthesis with one linker that contrasts the two sources in one sentence (one word, starting with w): The news site reports that 68% of young workers in Jakarta prefer hybrid work, ___ the HR report puts the figure at 41%.
assessment.rubric: Correct: whereas (contrasts two sources side by side in one sentence; the comma before it is fine). 'while' and 'whilst' (British) = 100. 'but' = 80 (grammatical and clear, but it doesn't start with w and is less formal for a report). 'however' = 40 (needs a full stop or a semicolon before it: '…hybrid work. However, the HR report …'). 'although' = 60 (grammatical, but it makes the second source sound like a small exception instead of an equal contrast). 'and' = 10 (hides the contradiction). Any answer that picks one figure or averages them = 0.

assessment.prompt: A practice statement from a city water company (invented) says: 'Setiap keluhan pelanggan akan ditindaklanjuti dalam waktu 3x24 jam.' Complete your English summary for a foreign client with the meaning of 'ditindaklanjuti' (two words): Every customer complaint will be ___ within 72 hours.
assessment.rubric: Correct: followed up (follow up a complaint = take the next action on it; 'followed up on' is common in American English). 'dealt with', 'acted on', 'looked into', 'responded to' = 100. 'handled' or 'addressed' = 100 (one word, but natural). 'processed' = 70. 'followed' alone = 30 (without 'up' it means 'came after'). 'continued' or 'follow-upped' = 10 (word-for-word from tindak lanjut). Wrong time (e.g. 24 hours) is not being tested here.

assessment.prompt: You're mediating between two colleagues at an NGO in Yogyakarta. Before you suggest anything, you restate one side's view neutrally, without giving your own opinion. Complete with one word: As I ___ it, Dimas wants to hire a new designer, while Rina would rather train someone in the team. Is that fair?
assessment.rubric: Correct: understand (As I understand it, … = this is what I heard from you; it restates, so it stays neutral). 'see' = 30 (As I see it = in my opinion: the mediator starts giving their own view). 'think' or 'believe' = 20 (your opinion, and 'As I think it' isn't natural). 'get' = 50 (understandable but not the fixed phrase). 'hear' = 60 (understandable; the natural phrases are 'As I understand it' or 'What I'm hearing is').

assessment.prompt: Pak Hasan wants the company conference in a big hotel in Jakarta; Dr. Wulan prefers a cheaper venue in Bandung. Both of them keep saying the conference must run smoothly for the guests. Complete the sentence that finds common ground (one word): It sounds like you both ___ the conference to run smoothly for our guests.
assessment.rubric: Correct: want (It sounds like you both want … : names what both sides agree on, before you look for a solution). 'need' = 100. 'would like' / 'expect' = 100. 'hope' = 50 (needs 'for': 'hope for the conference to run smoothly' is awkward; 'hope the conference runs smoothly' is natural). 'agree' = 20 (wrong pattern: 'agree the conference to run'). Any answer that takes one side = 0.

assessment.prompt: Anna, your Dutch manager in Jakarta, asks: 'Why didn't Dimas tell the director the deadline was impossible? He knew it was.' You explain: 'He felt uncomfortable contradicting someone so senior. Out of respect, he didn't want to cause problems for him or make him lose face, so he stayed quiet. It isn't shyness or fear.' Which Indonesian word are you explaining? Write it.
assessment.rubric: Correct: sungkan (a reluctance to bother, refuse or contradict someone, out of respect, often towards someone senior). 'segan' = 100 (very close in meaning). 'ewuh pakewuh' / 'pekewuh' (the Javanese idea) = 100. 'malu' = 40 (shame or shyness: the explanation says it isn't shyness). 'takut' = 10 (fear: the explanation says it isn't fear). 'basa-basi' or 'jam karet' = 0. An English word such as 'shy' or 'respect' = 20 (the item asks for the Indonesian concept).

assessment.prompt: Mark, a volunteer from Australia, asks how your village near Bandung decided where to build the new water tank. You explain: 'Nobody voted. The heads of the families talked it through over several meetings until everyone could accept one place. It's slower than a vote, but nobody feels left out.' Which Indonesian word describes this way of deciding? Write it.
assessment.rubric: Correct: musyawarah (a discussion that continues until the group reaches a consensus, often instead of a vote). 'musyawarah mufakat' / 'musyawarah untuk mufakat' = 100. 'mufakat' alone = 80 (that's the agreement they reach; the process is musyawarah). 'rapat' = 40 (any meeting, not this way of deciding). 'gotong royong' = 20 (working together for the community, not deciding). 'voting' = 0.

material.title: Synthesis: one summary from several sources

blocks.text:
Quick recap: at B1 a summary gave **the main point first** and **2–3 key facts**; at B2 you chose what to keep **for a particular reader**; at C1 reading you asked **who wrote it** and **what the evidence is**. Now you put several sources together. That's called **synthesis** (sintesis: menggabungkan beberapa sumber jadi satu teks).

The big rule: **organise by theme, not by source**. Don't write *Source A says … Source B says …* as two separate summaries. Take one point at a time and say what each source says about it:
- **Agreement:** *Both sources agree that … / Source A and Source B both report …*
- **Contrast:** *Source A suggests …, whereas Source B … / The sources disagree on …*
- **Gaps:** *Neither source mentions …*
- **Attribution** (saying who claims what): *According to the ministry's report, … / The news article reports that …*

Attribution matters most when the sources disagree: give **both figures and who gives them**. Don't silently pick one, and never average them.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat: di B1 ringkasan memberi **poin utama dulu** dan **2–3 fakta penting**; di B2 kamu memilih apa yang disimpan **untuk pembaca tertentu**; di pelajaran membaca C1 kamu bertanya **siapa penulisnya** dan **apa buktinya**. Sekarang kamu menggabungkan beberapa sumber. Itu disebut **synthesis** (sintesis: menggabungkan beberapa sumber jadi satu teks).

Aturan besarnya: **susun per tema, bukan per sumber**. Jangan menulis *Source A says … Source B says …* sebagai dua ringkasan terpisah. Ambil satu poin, lalu katakan apa kata masing-masing sumber tentang poin itu:
- **Kesamaan:** *Both sources agree that … / Source A and Source B both report …*
- **Perbedaan:** *Source A suggests …, whereas Source B … / The sources disagree on …*
- **Yang tidak dibahas:** *Neither source mentions …*
- **Atribusi** (menyebutkan siapa yang mengklaim apa): *According to the ministry's report, … / The news article reports that …*

Atribusi paling penting saat sumber-sumbernya berbeda: berikan **kedua angka dan siapa yang menyebutnya**. Jangan diam-diam memilih satu, dan jangan pernah merata-ratakannya.

blocks.text: Two practice sources (both invented). **Source A**, an Indonesian news site: 'Pemerintah kota akan melakukan sosialisasi program bank sampah di semua kelurahan mulai Mei. Menurut wali kota, 40% sampah rumah tangga bisa didaur ulang.' **Source B**, an English report by an environmental NGO: 'Waste bank programmes work best when residents get regular reminders. However, our survey found that only about 20% of household waste in the city can actually be recycled.' (A **waste bank**, bank sampah, is a place where residents bring sorted rubbish and get a little money for it; a **kelurahan** is an urban village, the smallest unit of city government.) A synthesis, theme by theme:

id.text: Dua sumber latihan (keduanya karangan). **Sumber A**, situs berita Indonesia: 'Pemerintah kota akan melakukan sosialisasi program bank sampah di semua kelurahan mulai Mei. Menurut wali kota, 40% sampah rumah tangga bisa didaur ulang.' **Sumber B**, laporan berbahasa Inggris dari sebuah LSM lingkungan: 'Waste bank programmes work best when residents get regular reminders. However, our survey found that only about 20% of household waste in the city can actually be recycled.' (**Waste bank** = bank sampah, tempat warga menyetor sampah yang sudah dipilah dan mendapat sedikit uang; **kelurahan** dijelaskan sebagai *an urban village*, unit pemerintahan kota yang paling kecil.) Sintesisnya, tema per tema:

rows.en: Both sources stress the need to inform residents: the city plans an awareness campaign from May, and the NGO says the programme works best with regular reminders.
rows.id: Kedua sumber menekankan perlunya memberi tahu warga: pemkot merencanakan sosialisasi mulai Mei, dan LSM itu mengatakan program ini paling berhasil dengan pengingat rutin.

id.note: tema 1: kesamaan

rows.en: However, they disagree on how much waste can be recycled: the mayor puts it at 40%, whereas the NGO's survey suggests only about 20%.
rows.id: Namun, keduanya berbeda soal berapa banyak sampah yang bisa didaur ulang: wali kota menyebut 40%, sedangkan survei LSM itu menunjukkan hanya sekitar 20%.
rows.note: theme 2: contrast, both figures with attribution

id.note: tema 2: perbedaan, kedua angka disertai sumbernya

rows.en: Neither source mentions how much the programme will cost.
rows.id: Tidak satu pun sumber menyebutkan berapa biaya programnya.
rows.note: a gap your reader may need to know about

id.note: hal yang tidak dibahas, mungkin perlu diketahui pembacamu

blocks.text:
Common mistakes:
- **Source by source** with no link: two mini-summaries, and the reader has to find the agreement and the contradiction alone.
- **No attribution:** *40% of household waste can be recycled.* Says who? Write *According to the mayor, …*
- **Picking or averaging figures:** report both, with their sources.
- **However with a comma:** `…40%, however the NGO says 20%` is wrong. Use *whereas / while* inside one sentence, or start a new sentence: *… 40%. However, the NGO …*
- **Mixing in your opinion:** keep the sources' claims and your own view (*In my view, …*) clearly apart.

id.text:
Kesalahan yang sering terjadi:
- **Sumber per sumber** tanpa penghubung: dua ringkasan mini, dan pembaca harus mencari sendiri kesamaan dan perbedaannya.
- **Tanpa atribusi:** *40% of household waste can be recycled.* Kata siapa? Tulis *According to the mayor, …*
- **Memilih atau merata-ratakan angka:** laporkan keduanya, beserta sumbernya.
- **However dengan koma:** `…40%, however the NGO says 20%` salah. Pakai *whereas / while* di dalam satu kalimat, atau mulai kalimat baru: *… 40%. However, the NGO …*
- **Mencampur opinimu:** pisahkan dengan jelas klaim sumber dan pandanganmu sendiri (*In my view, …*).

blocks.prompt: Two practice sources about a new MRT line: an Indonesian news report says it cut journey times by 30 minutes; an English consultancy report says the tickets are too expensive for many low-income workers. Which sentence is a synthesis?
options: The news report says the line cut journey times by 30 minutes. The consultancy report says the tickets are expensive.
The new line cuts journey times by 30 minutes, according to the news report, but the consultancy report warns that many low-income workers can't afford the tickets.
The new MRT line is fast but much too expensive.
blocks.explain: The middle sentence links the two sources in one point (the benefit and its limit) and says **who claims what**. The first is **source by source**, with no link between them, and the last has **no attribution**: it sounds like your own opinion.

id.prompt: Dua sumber latihan tentang jalur MRT baru: laporan berita Indonesia mengatakan jalur itu memangkas waktu perjalanan 30 menit; laporan konsultan berbahasa Inggris mengatakan tiketnya terlalu mahal bagi banyak pekerja berpenghasilan rendah. Kalimat mana yang merupakan sintesis?
id.explain: Kalimat tengah menghubungkan kedua sumber dalam satu poin (manfaat dan batasannya) dan menyebutkan **siapa yang mengklaim apa**. Kalimat pertama **sumber per sumber**, tanpa hubungan di antaranya, dan kalimat terakhir **tanpa atribusi**: terdengar seperti opinimu sendiri.

id.title: Sintesis: satu ringkasan dari beberapa sumber

material.title: Translate the meaning, not the words

blocks.text:
Indonesian government and office texts use a special style: long, formal, full of words like *sosialisasi, koordinasi, ditindaklanjuti, pihak terkait, dalam rangka*. Translated word for word, they turn into English that a foreign reader can't follow, or that means something else.

The biggest trap is **sosialisasi**. In English, **socialisation** means how a child learns to behave in society, or simply meeting people for fun. So *The ministry will do socialisation of the new rule* sounds very strange. Ask: **what will they actually do?** They will **inform the public**, **run an awareness campaign** or **explain the rule to residents**.

The same question works for every heavy phrase: **who does what, for whom?** Then say that in plain English.

id.text:
Teks pemerintahan dan kantor di Indonesia memakai gaya khusus: panjang, formal, penuh kata seperti *sosialisasi, koordinasi, ditindaklanjuti, pihak terkait, dalam rangka*. Kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata, hasilnya bahasa Inggris yang tidak bisa diikuti pembaca asing, atau malah artinya lain.

Jebakan terbesarnya **sosialisasi**. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **socialisation** berarti cara anak belajar berperilaku dalam masyarakat, atau sekadar bergaul untuk bersenang-senang. Jadi *The ministry will do socialisation of the new rule* terdengar sangat aneh. Tanyakan: **apa yang sebenarnya akan mereka lakukan?** Mereka akan **inform the public** (memberi tahu masyarakat), **run an awareness campaign** (mengadakan kampanye penyadaran) atau **explain the rule to residents** (menjelaskan aturannya kepada warga).

Pertanyaan yang sama berlaku untuk setiap frasa yang berat: **siapa melakukan apa, untuk siapa?** Lalu katakan itu dalam bahasa Inggris yang sederhana.

blocks.text:
- *Coordinate with* is fine English as a verb (*The agency will coordinate with the schools*); it's *do coordination* that isn't natural.
- **Follow up** a complaint (British) / **follow up on** a complaint (American): both are right. Without *up*, *follow* means *come after*.
- Spelling: **socialisation, programme** (British) / **socialization, program** (American). Pick one style and keep it.
- Translating meaning means you may need **more words** (*sosialisasi* → *an awareness campaign in schools and markets*) or **fewer** (*dalam rangka memperingati* → *to mark*).

id.text:
- *Coordinate with* sebagai kata kerja tetap benar dalam bahasa Inggris (*The agency will coordinate with the schools*); yang tidak alami adalah *do coordination*.
- **Follow up** a complaint (British) / **follow up on** a complaint (Amerika): dua-duanya benar. Tanpa *up*, *follow* berarti *datang sesudah*.
- Ejaan: **socialisation, programme** (British) / **socialization, program** (Amerika). Pilih satu gaya dan konsisten.
- Menerjemahkan makna berarti kadang butuh **lebih banyak kata** (*sosialisasi* → *an awareness campaign in schools and markets*) atau **lebih sedikit** (*dalam rangka memperingati* → *to mark*).

blocks.prompt: A practice announcement says: 'Kami akan berkoordinasi dengan pihak terkait.' Which English is the most natural for a foreign reader?
options: We will do coordination with the related parties.
We will socialise with the related sides.
We will work with the relevant agencies.
blocks.explain: Translate the meaning: *berkoordinasi dengan* = **work with** (or consult / coordinate with), and *pihak terkait* = **the relevant agencies**. *Do coordination* and *related parties* are word for word, and *socialise* means meeting people for fun.

id.prompt: Sebuah pengumuman latihan berbunyi: 'Kami akan berkoordinasi dengan pihak terkait.' Bahasa Inggris mana yang paling alami untuk pembaca asing?
id.explain: Terjemahkan maknanya: *berkoordinasi dengan* = **work with** (atau consult / coordinate with), dan *pihak terkait* = **the relevant agencies**. *Do coordination* dan *related parties* adalah terjemahan kata per kata, dan *socialise* berarti bergaul untuk bersenang-senang.

blocks.text:
At B2 you facilitated a group: you invited views and kept the task on track. Mediating is harder: two people **disagree**, and you help them reach something both can accept. A **mediator** (penengah) doesn't take sides. Five moves:
1. **Restate each side neutrally:** *So Budi's main concern is the cost, while Sari is worried about the deadline. Is that fair?* People calm down when they feel heard.
2. **Find common ground:** *It sounds like you both want the launch to go well.*
3. **Separate the people from the problem:** talk about the plan, the cost, the deadline, not about the person. No *you always / you never*, no loaded words (*stubborn, lazy*).
4. **Propose a way forward:** *What if we …? / How about …? / One option could be …*
5. **Check that both sides accept it:** *Can you both live with that?*

id.text:
Di B2 kamu memfasilitasi kelompok: mengajak orang berpendapat dan menjaga tugas tetap terarah. Memediasi lebih sulit: dua orang **berbeda pendapat**, dan kamu membantu mereka mencapai sesuatu yang bisa diterima keduanya. **Mediator** (penengah) tidak memihak. Lima langkah:
1. **Ulangi pendapat masing-masing dengan netral:** *So Budi's main concern is the cost, while Sari is worried about the deadline. Is that fair?* Orang jadi lebih tenang kalau merasa didengar.
2. **Cari titik temu:** *It sounds like you both want the launch to go well.*
3. **Pisahkan orangnya dari masalahnya:** bahas rencananya, biayanya, tenggatnya, bukan orangnya. Jangan pakai *you always / you never*, jangan pakai kata bermuatan (*stubborn, lazy*).
4. **Usulkan jalan keluar:** *What if we …? / How about …? / One option could be …*
5. **Pastikan kedua pihak menerimanya:** *Can you both live with that?*

rows.en: As I understand it, Sari would rather wait until everything works.

rows.en: We all agree that the client mustn't get a broken app.

id.note: jalan keluar

blocks.text:
Traps:
- **As I see it** and **In my opinion** give **your** view. To restate someone else's, say **As I understand it, …** or **So what you're saying is …**
- **Taking sides:** *Sari is right* ends your job as a mediator.
- **Calm down** sounds rude and makes people angrier: restate their point instead.
- *Yang penting sama-sama enak* → **The important thing is that it works for everyone**, not `the important is same-same nice`.

Culture: in many Indonesian teams people avoid open disagreement, especially with someone senior (they feel *sungkan*). A mediator may talk to each side privately first, and invite the quieter person by name.

id.text:
Jebakan:
- **As I see it** dan **In my opinion** menyampaikan pandangan**mu** sendiri. Untuk mengulang pendapat orang lain, katakan **As I understand it, …** atau **So what you're saying is …**
- **Memihak:** *Sari is right* mengakhiri peranmu sebagai mediator.
- **Calm down** terdengar kasar dan membuat orang makin marah: lebih baik ulangi poin mereka.
- *Yang penting sama-sama enak* → **The important thing is that it works for everyone**, bukan `the important is same-same nice`.

Budaya: di banyak tim di Indonesia orang menghindari perbedaan pendapat secara terbuka, terutama dengan orang yang lebih senior (mereka merasa *sungkan*). Mediator bisa berbicara dengan masing-masing pihak secara pribadi dulu, dan mengajak orang yang lebih pendiam dengan menyebut namanya.

blocks.prompt: Budi wants to cut the training budget; Sari says the new staff need the training. You're mediating. Which sentence separates the people from the problem?
options: Budi, you always ignore what the staff need.
The budget and the training are pulling in different directions, so let's look at both.
Sari, you're being too emotional about this.
blocks.explain: The middle sentence makes **the problem** (the budget and the training) the subject, so nobody is blamed. The other two attack **the person**: *you always ignore* and *too emotional* are judgements, and they make the disagreement worse.

id.prompt: Budi ingin memangkas anggaran pelatihan; Sari bilang karyawan baru butuh pelatihan itu. Kamu yang memediasi. Kalimat mana yang memisahkan orangnya dari masalahnya?
id.explain: Kalimat tengah menjadikan **masalahnya** (anggaran dan pelatihan) sebagai subjek (pelaku kalimat), jadi tidak ada yang disalahkan. Dua kalimat lainnya menyerang **orangnya**: *you always ignore* dan *too emotional* adalah penilaian, dan membuat perselisihannya makin buruk.

blocks.text:
At B1 you explained words like *mudik* and *arisan* with *It's a kind of …* and *It's when …*. Some ideas need more, because they're about values and feelings, and **no single English word** fits. Use four parts:
1. **An approximate translation:** *Roughly, it means … / The closest English word is …, but …*
2. **An example** from real life.
3. **What it isn't:** *It isn't just … / It's more than …* This stops the wrong English word from sticking.
4. **Why it matters** for the listener: *That's why … / So if …*

Keep the Indonesian word (in italics when you write), and say it **neutrally**: explain, don't judge, and don't turn it into a stereotype.

id.text:
Di B1 kamu menjelaskan kata seperti *mudik* dan *arisan* dengan *It's a kind of …* dan *It's when …*. Sebagian konsep butuh lebih dari itu, karena menyangkut nilai dan perasaan, dan **tidak ada satu kata bahasa Inggris** yang pas. Pakai empat bagian:
1. **Terjemahan kira-kira:** *Roughly, it means … / The closest English word is …, but …*
2. **Contoh** dari kehidupan nyata.
3. **Apa yang bukan:** *It isn't just … / It's more than …* Ini mencegah kata bahasa Inggris yang salah menempel di kepala pendengar.
4. **Kenapa itu penting** bagi pendengarnya: *That's why … / So if …*

Pertahankan kata Indonesianya (miring kalau ditulis), dan sampaikan dengan **netral**: jelaskan, jangan menghakimi, dan jangan jadikan stereotip.

rows.en: Gotong royong is roughly community mutual help: neighbours work together for free, like cleaning the drains on a Sunday.
rows.id: Gotong royong kira-kira berarti saling bantu dalam masyarakat: tetangga bekerja bersama tanpa dibayar, misalnya membersihkan selokan hari Minggu.
rows.note: more than 'teamwork': unpaid, for everyone, nobody is the boss

id.note: lebih dari 'teamwork': tanpa bayaran, untuk semua, tidak ada bosnya

rows.en: Sungkan is a reluctance to bother or contradict someone, out of respect. It isn't shyness.
rows.id: Sungkan adalah rasa enggan merepotkan atau membantah seseorang, karena hormat. Itu bukan rasa malu.

id.note: tidak ada satu kata padanan bahasa Inggris

rows.en: Musyawarah is a discussion that goes on until everyone can accept the decision, often instead of a vote.
rows.id: Musyawarah adalah diskusi yang berlanjut sampai semua orang bisa menerima keputusannya, sering kali sebagai pengganti voting.

id.note: kesepakatan yang dicapai = mufakat

rows.en: Jam karet, or 'rubber time', means start times can be flexible at some informal events. Work meetings usually start on time.
rows.id: Jam karet, atau 'waktu karet', berarti jam mulai bisa fleksibel di sebagian acara santai. Rapat kerja biasanya mulai tepat waktu.

id.note: netral, bukan 'Indonesians are always late'

rows.en: Mudik is the trip back to your hometown for Lebaran. Millions travel at once, so tickets sell out weeks before.
rows.id: Mudik adalah perjalanan pulang ke kampung halaman untuk Lebaran. Jutaan orang bepergian bersamaan, jadi tiket habis berminggu-minggu sebelumnya.
rows.note: not just 'going home', which sounds like after work

id.note: bukan sekadar 'going home', yang terdengar seperti pulang kerja

rows.en: Basa-basi is polite small talk. 'Sudah makan?' is a friendly greeting, not an invitation to lunch.
rows.id: Basa-basi adalah obrolan ringan untuk sopan santun. 'Sudah makan?' adalah sapaan ramah, bukan ajakan makan siang.
rows.note: not 'fake talk': it builds the relationship

id.note: bukan 'omong kosong': itu menjaga hubungan

blocks.text:
One wrong English word can stick for years. Watch out for:
- **sungkan ≠ shy:** a confident manager can feel *sungkan* towards a director.
- **gotong royong ≠ teamwork:** teamwork happens at work, for pay; gotong royong is unpaid, for the community.
- **basa-basi ≠ fake:** it's polite, not dishonest.
- **mudik ≠ go home:** *go home* sounds like after work. Say *travel back to your hometown for Lebaran*.

And keep it neutral: *Indonesians are always late* is a stereotype; *At some informal events, start times are flexible* is an explanation.

id.text:
Satu kata bahasa Inggris yang salah bisa menempel bertahun-tahun. Hati-hati dengan:
- **sungkan ≠ shy:** manajer yang percaya diri pun bisa merasa *sungkan* kepada direktur.
- **gotong royong ≠ teamwork:** teamwork terjadi di tempat kerja, dibayar; gotong royong tanpa bayaran, untuk masyarakat.
- **basa-basi ≠ fake:** itu sopan santun, bukan ketidakjujuran.
- **mudik ≠ go home:** *go home* terdengar seperti pulang kerja. Katakan *travel back to your hometown for Lebaran*.

Dan tetap netral: *Indonesians are always late* adalah stereotip; *At some informal events, start times are flexible* adalah penjelasan.

blocks.prompt: Lukas, an intern from Germany, asks: 'Is it true that Indonesians are always late?' Which answer explains jam karet best?
options: Yes, we call it jam karet. Nobody here cares about time.
People sometimes joke about jam karet, 'rubber time': at some informal events the start time is flexible. But work meetings, flights and exams start on time.
No, that's completely wrong. Indonesians are never late.
blocks.explain: The middle answer gives the **approximate translation** ('rubber time'), says **where** it happens and **what it isn't** (work meetings start on time), all in a **neutral** tone. The first confirms a stereotype, and the last denies something every Indonesian knows exists.

id.prompt: Lukas, mahasiswa magang dari Jerman, bertanya: 'Is it true that Indonesians are always late?' Jawaban mana yang paling baik menjelaskan jam karet?
id.explain: Jawaban tengah memberi **terjemahan kira-kira** ('rubber time'), menyebutkan **di mana** itu terjadi dan **apa yang bukan** (rapat kerja mulai tepat waktu), semuanya dengan nada **netral**. Jawaban pertama membenarkan stereotip, dan jawaban terakhir menyangkal sesuatu yang semua orang Indonesia tahu memang ada.

Levelnya B2, jadi lebih mudah dari pelajaran ini, dengan transkrip dan latihan.

id.intro: Di B2 kamu meringkas satu artikel panjang untuk pembaca tertentu dan menjaga kelompok tetap bekerja sama. Sekarang tugasnya lebih besar: menggabungkan beberapa sumber, sebagian berbahasa Indonesia dan sebagian berbahasa Inggris, jadi satu ringkasan bahasa Inggris yang jelas; membantu dua rekan kerja yang berbeda pendapat menemukan jalan keluar; dan menjelaskan konsep Indonesia seperti gotong royong dan sungkan sampai rekan kerja asing benar-benar memahaminya.

assessment.syn-1: Sebuah artikel berita latihan (karangan) berbunyi: 'Pemerintah kota akan melakukan sosialisasi aturan label gula pada minuman kemasan di sekolah-sekolah dan pasar selama bulan Maret, sebelum aturan itu berlaku 1 April.' Kamu menulis ringkasan berbahasa Inggris untuk sebuah LSM kesehatan internasional. Lengkapi dengan satu kata bahasa Inggris: In March, the city will run a public ___ campaign about the new sugar labels in schools and markets, before the rule starts on 1 April.
assessment.syn-2: Sumber A, situs berita Indonesia (teks latihan): 'Survei kami: 68% pekerja muda di Jakarta lebih memilih kerja hybrid.' Sumber B, laporan berbahasa Inggris dari konsultan SDM (teks latihan): 'Only 41% of young workers in Jakarta said they preferred hybrid work.' Lengkapi sintesisnya dengan satu kata penghubung bahasa Inggris yang mempertentangkan kedua sumber dalam satu kalimat (satu kata, diawali huruf w): The news site reports that 68% of young workers in Jakarta prefer hybrid work, ___ the HR report puts the figure at 41%.
assessment.syn-3: Pernyataan latihan dari perusahaan air minum kota (karangan) berbunyi: 'Setiap keluhan pelanggan akan ditindaklanjuti dalam waktu 3x24 jam.' Lengkapi ringkasan bahasa Inggrismu untuk klien asing dengan makna 'ditindaklanjuti' (dua kata bahasa Inggris): Every customer complaint will be ___ within 72 hours.
assessment.syn-4: Kamu menengahi dua rekan kerja di sebuah LSM di Yogyakarta. Sebelum mengusulkan apa pun, kamu mengulang pendapat mereka dengan netral, tanpa memberi opinimu sendiri. Lengkapi dengan satu kata bahasa Inggris: As I ___ it, Dimas wants to hire a new designer, while Rina would rather train someone in the team. Is that fair?
assessment.syn-5: Pak Hasan ingin konferensi perusahaan diadakan di hotel besar di Jakarta; Dr. Wulan lebih memilih tempat yang lebih murah di Bandung. Keduanya terus mengatakan konferensinya harus berjalan lancar untuk para tamu. Lengkapi kalimat untuk menemukan titik temu (satu kata bahasa Inggris): It sounds like you both ___ the conference to run smoothly for our guests.
assessment.syn-6: Anna, manajermu dari Belanda di Jakarta, bertanya: 'Why didn't Dimas tell the director the deadline was impossible? He knew it was.' Kamu menjelaskan: 'He felt uncomfortable contradicting someone so senior. Out of respect, he didn't want to cause problems for him or make him lose face, so he stayed quiet. It isn't shyness or fear.' Kata bahasa Indonesia apa yang sedang kamu jelaskan? Tuliskan.
assessment.syn-7: Mark, relawan dari Australia, bertanya bagaimana desamu di dekat Bandung memutuskan lokasi tandon air yang baru. Kamu menjelaskan: 'Nobody voted. The heads of the families talked it through over several meetings until everyone could accept one place. It's slower than a vote, but nobody feels left out.' Kata bahasa Indonesia apa yang menggambarkan cara memutuskan seperti ini? Tuliskan.
